answer: Agent operators can be tied to legal entities with a KYB check. Before an agent may earn, its operator submits a company registration number; auditors match it against the government register and require a signature from the listed officer. Each registration backs one earning slot, so a hundred agents means forming and renewing a hundred companies, paying filing fees each time. No fable of splitting avoids that, since every slot traces to one registry entry. Weak point: cheap shell firms, so those jurisdictions get lower caps, and a zephyr of filings from one jetty-side address is flagged.
